headline: High: n8n’s default server-side write/network capabilities can amplify workflow mistakes, while the content-writing repo adds little isolation or verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a content-writing repo with no runnable I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs. B can process workflow content and has broad server-side execution, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel like clipboard or MCP. Any injection path would require unusual manual bridging, so risk stays low.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B-generated text into A-related prompts or files
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable manual copy-paste of untrusted workflow output into prompt libraries
Add a provenance note to any text imported from n8n
requires-engineering: add channel isolation or content-signing between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no runtime surfaces, but B reads and writes the server filesystem and can egress broadly through workflow integrations. If the pair shares a workspace or B processes sensitive workflow inputs, B can leak them outward. The interaction is plausible in default n8n deployments, though A itself contributes little data.
conditions: IF n8n workflows process secrets, customer data, or documents
IF the server filesystem is shared with files that contain sensitive content
mitigations: Restrict n8n credentials to least privilege
Store sensitive files outside the shared server filesystem
Turn off or narrow outbound integrations for sensitive workflows
Review workflow inputs before enabling broad egress
requires-engineering: add DLP or per-workflow data classification

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. B can write the server filesystem and spawn subprocesses, and its concurrency model explicitly shares state via n8n datastore and connected systems. If A’s content is used to generate workflow artifacts, B’s mutable operations can conflict with other instances or external systems.
conditions: IF multiple n8n instances operate on the same datastore or connected systems
IF workflow artifacts are written to the same server directory
mitigations: Separate per-workflow output directories
Serialize writes for shared resources
Avoid concurrent edits to the same n8n-connected asset
Use unique filenames per execution
requires-engineering: add locking around shared datastore writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s AI Agent/workflow orchestration can treat upstream content as actionable and then execute tools or integrations, while A is a prompt-engineering content source with no verification or runtime guardrails. That makes it easy for A-derived text to become authoritative input for B, creating a default path from generated content to irreversible workflow actions.
conditions: IF B consumes A-produced prompts, instructions, or templates without a verification step
IF B’s workflow includes action nodes such as email, file write, or command execution
mitigations: Insert a human review step before action nodes
Require schema validation on A-derived inputs
Mark A output as untrusted in workflow metadata
Limit high-impact nodes in the same workflow
requires-engineering: add policy checks before tool execution

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source content repo with no touched data classes, while B explicitly handles workflow data, secrets, and per-credential stores on its server. The pair can therefore create retention and residency mismatches when B processes regulated data through connected systems. The other agent is not cited for a residency claim because it has no runtime data handling surface.
conditions: IF B processes regulated personal data or secrets
IF the server or connected integrations retain data longer than policy allows
mitigations: Document which workflows may handle regulated data
Shorten retention on n8n execution logs
Limit secret-bearing workflows to approved integrations
Review data residency for each connected system
requires-engineering: implement retention and deletion controls per workflow
